rows.hook: Unwinding shorts pushes currency higher

modes.bear: Rapid currency appreciation hurts export-heavy sectors like IT and pharma, potentially dampening their near-term earnings.
modes.bull: Foreign inflows into Indian stocks signal strong confidence, driving the rupee higher and reducing imported inflation pressures.
modes.simple: The Indian rupee gained strength against the US dollar because foreign investors bought local stocks and closed out bearish bets.

This appreciation reflects sudden capital inflows into the Indian stock market, relieving some pressure on local asset valuations. Retail investors holding import-heavy stocks or export businesses should note how currency swings impact corporate margins. Tracking currency stability remains critical for assessing foreign institutional investor sentiment in domestic markets.
